title: Project plan: the Riverside Community Kitchen
sections: This plan authorises the Riverside Community Kitchen. Its objective: Open a community kitchen that serves 200 meals a week. The sponsor is Riverside Trust. The declared budget is USD 48,000.00. The critical path runs 50 periods, with 4 critical activities. The plan carries the charter, scope, work breakdown, schedule, cost, assignments and risks; a record that is missing is named rather than guessed.

The charter authorises the Riverside Community Kitchen under Riverside Trust. The project manager is Alex Rivera. The declared budget is USD 48,000.00. Work starts on 2026-01-05. It is due on 2026-06-30.
| Objective | Open a community kitchen that serves 200 meals a week. |
The scope declares 2 included items, 1 exclusion and 2 deliverables. The WBS decomposes the deliverables; the exclusions bound the work the project will not do.
The WBS carries 4 nodes and 4 work packages. Each work package states an owner, a cost and the test that shows it is complete; the parent nodes carry the roll-up.
| ID | Work package | Owner | Cost | Acceptance |
| A1 | Design the kitchen | Architect | USD 6,000.00 | Drawings signed |
| A2 | Apply for the permit | Project manager | USD 2,000.00 | Permit issued |
| A3 | Fit out the kitchen | Builder | USD 30,000.00 | Handover signed |
| A4 | Install equipment | Supplier | USD 10,000.00 | Equipment commissioned |

The schedule carries 4 activities. The critical path runs 50 periods and carries 4 critical activities. Early and late dates and float are the frozen method's own values; an activity with float is not on the critical path.
| ID | Activity | Duration | ES | EF | LS | LF | Float | Critical |

The WBS rolls 4 nodes up to a total of USD 48,000.00. The declared budget is USD 48,000.00; the variance is USD 0.00. Cost is carried by the work package, not by the activity; no estimate is added where the record declares none.
| A2 | Apply for the permit | USD 2,000.00 |
| A3 | Fit out the kitchen | USD 30,000.00 |

The plan names 4 resources. Every activity carries exactly one accountable role and at least one responsible role in the RACI matrix; a blank cell or a missing role is a named gap, not an inferred assignment.
| Activity | Name | Design | Management | Build | Equipment |
The register carries 1 risk. Likelihood and impact are labels, not probabilities, and each risk states a response and an owner. No risk score or expected loss is computed.
| ID | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Response | Owner |
| R1 | Permit delay | Medium | High | Apply early | Project manager |
Progress is judged against 1 success measure, 1 assumption and 1 constraint. A success measure without a baseline is reported as stated, not converted into a target.
| 200 meals a week by month six | success measure |
| The lease is signed before work starts | assumption |
| The kitchen must open before June | constraint |

The plan is limited to the record the student supplied. The CPM uses the declared single-point durations; PERT was not run unless the record asks for it. Costs are work-package estimates, not commitments. The plan does not assess procurement, financing or benefits beyond the declared success measures, and it does not rank the risks. The schedule and cost are tied to the WBS as recorded, so a changed scope changes both and must follow the change-control route above. A reader should treat the named gaps as open questions, not as conditions already met.

The plan states what the project delivers, how it is broken down, what it costs, who does the work and what could go wrong. The WBS rolls up to USD 48,000.00 against a declared budget of USD 48,000.00. The critical path is 50 periods over 4 activities.
